docs.title: pydump
docs.text:
Structured dump and die for Python scripts and CLIs. Stdlib only. No browser, no web framework required.

Rich terminal trees — ANSI colors when stderr is a TTY

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
Built for plain Python. Need HTML in the browser? Use pydd.

  • Python / CLI

    Stdlib only — scripts, tests, CI

  • Need web? → pydd

    FastAPI · Flask · Django HTML dumps

  • Install

    pip install pydump-dd

    Installation guide

  • Get started

    Dump a dict in three lines.

docs.title: Quick example
docs.text:
import pydump  # installs dd/dump as builtins

user = {"id": 1, "name": "Ada", "roles": ["admin", "editor"]}
dump(user)   # stderr, keep running
dd(user)     # stderr, then exit 1

docs.title: Public functions
docs.text: Function Description dump(*args, **kwargs) Write formatted dump to stderr, continue execution dd(*args, **kwargs) Same as dump, then SystemExit(1) render_text(*args, color=None, **kwargs) Return dump string; no I/O, no exit configure(project_root=...) Base path for relative // file:line tips install_helpers() Inject dd / dump into builtins (auto on import pydump)

docs.title: Lower-level helpers
docs.text:
For custom formatters (used internally by pydd HTML):

Symbol Description inspect_value(value) Walk a value → DumpNode tree DumpNode Dataclass representing one dump fragment set_project_root(path) Same as configure at module level caller_frame() Call-site frame for tip paths caller_arg_names() AST-inferred variable names from call line format_dump_tip(...) Build tip string: file:line · $var · kind · type describe_value(value) Human-readable kind/type metadata value_kind(value) / value_type_name(value) Type classification helpers

docs.title: DumpNode schema
docs.text:
@dataclass
class DumpNode:
    kind: str       # scalar | container | object | recursion | truncated
    label: str = ''
    text: str = ''
    scalar_kind: str = ''
    children: list[tuple[str, DumpNode]] = field(default_factory=list)

docs.title: Demo
docs.text: Runnable examples for terminal dumps.

docs.title: Basic dict dump
docs.text:
debug.py:

import pydump

payload = {
    "id": 1,
    "author": "Jane Doe",
    "title": "Hello world",
    "tags": ["python", "debug", "pydump"],
}

dump(payload)

Run:

pip install pydump-dd
python debug.py

Output:

dict:4 [
  "id" => 1
  "author" => "Jane Doe"
  "title" => "Hello world"
  "tags" => list:3 [
    0 => "python"
    1 => "debug"
    2 => "pydump"
  ]
] // debug.py:12

docs.title: Dump and die
docs.text:
from pydump import dd

dd({"status": "fatal", "code": 42})
# prints dump, then process exits with code 1

docs.title: Multiple values
docs.text:
from pydump import dd

user = {"id": 1}
post = {"title": "Hello"}
dd(user, post, request_id=99)

Each value gets its own dump block with separate tips.

docs.title: Class and function introspection
docs.text:
from pydump import dump

def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}"

class User:
    id: int = 1
    name: str = "Ada"

dump(greet)
dump(User)

Shows name, module, signature, bases, and public attributes.

docs.title: Plain text for CI
docs.text:
NO_COLOR=1 python debug.py

Or in code:

from pydump import render_text
print(render_text(data, color=False))

docs.title: Custom formatter (advanced)
docs.text:
Build on the shared inspection core:

from pydump import inspect_value, DumpNode

node = inspect_value({"a": [1, 2, 3]})

def walk(n: DumpNode, indent=0):
    print("  " * indent + n.label)
    for key, child in n.children:
        print("  " * indent + f"{key}:")
        walk(child, indent + 1)

walk(node)

This is how pydd builds HTML output.

docs.title: Core capabilities
docs.text:
• Zero dependencies — stdlib only; easy to ship in any project
  • Terminal-first — full tree expansion in logs (no fake collapse UI)
  • Readable structure — "key" => value layout with typed labels (dict:3, list:2)
  • Call-site tips — $variable · kind · type and // file:line on dump header
  • ANSI colors — 24-bit colors when stderr is a TTY; respects NO_COLOR
  • Laravel-style globals — import pydump injects dd / dump into builtins
  • Multiple values — positional and keyword args each get a dump block
  • Max depth guard — default depth 4 prevents hangs on huge objects (e.g. SQLAlchemy)
  • Cycle detection — shows <recursion TypeName> for circular references
  • Shared core — same DumpNode tree powers pydd HTML output

docs.title: What gets inspected
docs.text: Value type Output dict Keyed children, dict:N label list / tuple / set Indexed children, typed label class Module, bases, public attributes function / method Name, module, signature, source file object instance Public __dict__ / __slots__ (non-callable, no _ prefix) scalars None, bool, int, float, str (str truncated at 160 chars)

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Effect NO_COLOR=1 Plain text output FORCE_COLOR=1 Force ANSI even when stderr is not a TTY

docs.title: Use cases
docs.text:
• Scripts and one-off tools
  • Management commands
  • Tests and notebooks (careful with dd() — it exits)
  • CI logs (NO_COLOR=1 recommended)

docs.title: What pydump is not
docs.text:
Limitations

  • No HTML — browser dumps require pydd
  • dd() stops the process — not for production error handling
  • No syntax highlighting — colored text, not source-highlighted code
  • Private attrs skipped — by design on object instances
  • Depth capped — very deep structures show truncation markers

docs.title: Relationship to pydd
docs.text:
pydump   → terminal (this package)
pydd     → pydump + HTML + FastAPI / Flask / Django

Installing pydd-web automatically installs pydump-dd. For CLI-only projects, depend on pydump-dd directly.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: Get readable terminal dumps in under two minutes.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text: pip install pydump-dd

docs.title: 2. Create a script
docs.text:
main.py:

import pydump  # Laravel-style: dd/dump available everywhere after this

user = {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "Ada",
    "roles": ["admin", "editor"],
}

dump(user)   # print to stderr, keep running

docs.title: 3. Run
docs.text:
python main.py

Expected output:

dict:3 [
  "id" => 1
  "name" => "Ada"
  "roles" => list:2 [
    0 => "admin"
    1 => "editor"
  ]
] // main.py:9

docs.title: 4. Dump and die
docs.text:
dd(user)  # same output, then exit code 1

Use dd() when you want to stop after inspecting — like Laravel's dd().

Warning

dd() raises SystemExit(1). Do not use in production request handlers.

docs.title: 5. Explicit imports (optional)
docs.text:
from pydump import dd, dump, render_text, configure

Better for type checkers and IDEs.
